No Result View All Result Home News Politics Business Sport Football Health Entertainment Education Opinion Editorial Columns Others LeVogue Magazine Conferences National Economy Contact Us Hausa Edition Home News Politics Business Sport Football Health Entertainment Education Opinion Editorial Columns Others LeVogue Magazine Conferences National Economy Contact Us No Result View All Result No Result View All Result Nigeria Must Be Bigger Than Any Political Party, Individual — Jonathan Tells Ex-Deputy Governors by Ruth Nwokwu 7 minutes ago in Cover Stories , News Share on WhatsApp Share on Facebook Share on X Telegram Former President Goodluck Jonathan has urged Nigerian leaders to place national unity and the country’s interests above political parties, individuals and sectional interests, saying the country’s future depends on responsible leadership and collective commitment to democracy.
Jonathan made the call at the fifth annual conference of the Forum of Former Deputy Governors of Nigeria, where the Deputy Governor of Adamawa State, Bala Ngilari, represented him.
In his address, Jonathan described the forum as a unique platform capable of contributing significantly to national unity and democratic growth, given the diversity of its members in terms of political affiliation and geographical representation.
“Nigeria must always be bigger than any political party or individual, regional or sectional interest,” he said.
He noted that former deputy governors occupied an important position in the country’s political system, having served at the intersection of political parties, government and the citizens they represented.
“The forum is unique and can play a significant role in national unity and the growth of democracy in Nigeria because the deputy governors are from different political parties and come from different parts of Nigeria,” Jonathan said.
He urged members of the forum to sustain their commitment to national development even after leaving public office, stressing that their responsibilities to the country did not end with the expiration of their tenures.
“While we serve as deputy governors, we must serve as major links between our political parties and our citizens. Now that we are out of service, we must continue,” he said.
Jonathan emphasised the need for former public officeholders to mentor younger Nigerians, urging them to provide guidance that would help the next generation make responsible decisions and contribute meaningfully to society.
“Our responsibilities did not end when we left office. We have a duty to mentor young ones in Nigeria to do what is right even when it is difficult,” he said.
According to the former president, young Nigerians require more than opportunities to succeed; they also need guidance from experienced leaders to navigate challenges and avoid mistakes that could affect their future.
“Our young people need more than opportunities to succeed. If we fail to guide them, we allow them to make avoidable mistakes,” he said.
Jonathan also identified Nigeria’s human resources as the country’s greatest asset, describing Nigerians as creative, hardworking and resilient.
“Our greatest asset is our people. Nigerians are creative, hardworking and resilient,” he said.
He cautioned political leaders against treating public office as a permanent position, noting that although political appointments and tenures eventually end, the consequences of decisions taken while in office can affect generations.
“Political office is temporary, but the consequences of our decisions will remain for generations,” he said.
